How to read this document

This is a reasoning surface, not an exhaustive corpus export or a literature survey. It is designed to expose the principal premises, obstructions, and open interfaces before work begins. The machine-readable corpus remains the current inventory when later theorem waves outrun this exposition. Three conventions carry the paper’s claim boundary.

Every statement is tagged. [Lean] means a proof term was checked by the pinned Lean kernel. [Cert] means an exact finite computation, with no floating-point decision anywhere in it. [Math] means proved in ordinary mathematics in the sources but not formalised. [Cited] means established in the published literature. [Open] means not proved. These are never blurred, and a statement carrying one band is never described in language belonging to another.

Every parameter-indexed statement is tagged scale:fixed (proved at specific listed values), scale:bounded (proved below an explicit bound), scale:cofinal (proved for arbitrarily large parameters), or scale:uniform (proved for all parameters). The corpus contains theorems at all four scales; the unresolved endpoint depends on a particular cofinal certificate producer that is not among them. Sorting by scale keeps that distinction visible.

Every statement records the representation it is expressed in. An obstruction is a fact about a coordinate, not about the object, and a wall measured in one representation may simply not exist in another; the atlas section gives the transport maps, so any obstruction recorded here can be re-measured elsewhere.

Erdős Problem 249 is open. No section of this document claims otherwise, and a reduction of the problem to another statement is recorded as a reduction, never as progress toward a solution.

The problem, and what is actually known

Let φ\varphi be Euler’s totient function and put S:=∑n≥1φ(n)2n=12+14+28+216+432+⋯=1.3676308019850223…S \;:=\; \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{\varphi(n)}{2^{n}} \;=\; \tfrac12 + \tfrac14 + \tfrac{2}{8} + \tfrac{2}{16} + \tfrac{4}{32} + \cdots \;=\; 1.3676308019850223\ldots The series converges absolutely because φ(n)≤n\varphi(n) \le n. Erdős Problem #249 asks whether SS is irrational. Nothing in this document decides it, no route recorded here is a proof, and no result here should be read as an approach that is close to working. What this document does is different in kind: it assembles every recorded failure, obstruction, countermodel and dead route the programme has produced against #249, and classifies each one by the exact class of argument it eliminates. The claim being made is that those failures are not independent — they are repeated measurements of a single obstruction, and that obstruction has a shape which can be stated.

The open question has a sharp equivalent inside the corpus, and it is the statement everything below is measured against. Propositions – are the four facts a reader should carry into the next section: the corpus’s best cofinal information is half a certificate, its best rank information runs the wrong way, its reformulations are equivalences rather than reductions, and every purely qualitative property of the coefficient word is satisfied by a rational countermodel.

The wall

This programme has produced many exact reformulations of #249 and no proof. That is the honest summary, and the rest of this section is an argument that it is also the wrong way to read the record. The reformulations do not fail independently. They fail in a small number of recurring ways, and when each failure is stated as a claim about rather than as a report that something did not work, the classes fit together into one obstruction with a describable shape. A hundred reformulations that all die are not a hundred failures; they are a hundred measurements of one wall, taken from different angles. The measurements are below.

The thesis, in one sentence:

The plane the barriers live on

Fix two axes for a hypothetical proof of Sep\mathrm{Sep} (Definition ): the of indices at which it consults φ\varphi, and the at which it consults them. Two derived axes matter as well: the size of the proof’s internal bookkeeping (carry state, ℚ\mathbb{Q}-rank, shift-polynomial degree), and whether the target is asserted at a chosen index or as an over a block.

  • The quadrant [full resolution ×\times bounded range] is closed by Theorem  (B1): φ\varphi may be pinned exactly on [1,B][1,B] and the series can still be rational.

  • The complementary quadrant [coarse resolution ×\times unbounded range] is closed by Proposition  (B7): φ\varphi’s parity may be pinned at index, together with boundedness, c(n)≤nc(n) \le n, and arbitrarily strong aperiodicity, and the series can still be 3/23/2.

  • The remaining quadrant is closed : B5 (no bounded carry state, no fixed-precision signature) and B6 (four independent finite truncations of the totient kernel, all with trivial kernel).

  • B4 closes the one construction that tried to reach the good quadrant by values: residue engineering pays for amplitude in position, and position enters the certificate radius.

  • B2 closes the escape of retargeting; B3 records that no bounded result in the corpus has ever promoted.

The corpus’s own results partition along these axes perfectly, which is the first evidence that the axes are the right ones. Every unconditional deposit (Proposition , the K=240K=240 Farey rung of Theorem , the actual-LCM orbits at a=4a = 4 and a=6a = 6) sits at full resolution and bounded range, so B1 says extending them is evidence forever and proof never. Every unconditional theorem (letterwise positivity for all a≥8a \ge 8, the tail bounds from φ(m)≤m\varphi(m) \le m, unbounded Mersenne-shadow denominator growth) sits at coarse resolution and unbounded range, and Proposition  proves in the corpus’s own coordinate that this is exactly half a certificate.

Corollary 13 (What B1 rules out). No proof rule that is uniform over all coefficient sequences c(n)≤nc(n)\le n can establish Sep\mathrm{Sep} from a single fixed prefix {c(n):n≤B}\{c(n):n\le B\}: Theorem  supplies a rational countermodel with that same prefix. This does invalidate an argument that uses the fixed arithmetic sequence φ\varphi together with compatible information at arbitrarily large horizons; the theorem gives a different γB\gamma_B for each BB, not one sequence agreeing with φ\varphi at every BB.

Remark 14 (Scope discipline — what B1 does say). Theorem  is a statement about proof method, not about φ\varphi. It does not touch SS, and it does not suggest that φ\varphi is such a γ\gamma; it says only that no fixed-horizon check can tell them apart. It also does kill bounded-parameter certificates in general. “Bounded parameter” splits into four independent bounds with four different killers: bounded index range (this theorem), bounded certificate depth LL (killed separately, and by a Lean theorem — certifiedKill_depth_floor\mathrm{certifiedKill\_depth\_floor} forces 2(N+h+L+2)<2L2(N{+}h{+}L{+}2) < 2^{L}), bounded proof state (B5), and bounded rank (B6). Conflating them would overstate B1.

The Lean-formalised sibling of the same mechanism — a lacunary zero-valued coboundary splice — is Proposition , which is B7. B1 and B7 are the two object-level witnesses of the wall, one along each axis.

B2–B7

Each barrier below is stated as a claim about a class of arguments, with its status never blurred. means there is a theorem (Lean or ordinary mathematics, as marked) whose content is the elimination. means an audit over the corpus: real evidence, not a theorem, and it is never used as a premise elsewhere in this document.

Proposition 15 (B2, route-collapse: intermediate targets are not waypoints). Status: proved (Lean, three independent mechanisms).

  1. Every certificate vocabulary is an with the underlying non-integrality, so every re-encoding of Sep\mathrm{Sep} is equivalent to Sep\mathrm{Sep} (, forward at :132, converse at :143).

  2. Any weakening in which the prover may which indices to test collapses to Irrational(S)\mathrm{Irrational}(S) outright, because irrationality plus doubling expansivity already supplies a two-point sample with the required separation (). The mechanism is visible in the converse proof (windowSeparatedPairsAt_of_cofinally_scaled_adjacent_chord, PivotAntiReconstruction.lean:1663): it selects T={N,N+1}T = \{N, N+1\} and two ordered pairs, and the counted-energy threshold 2|T|2/5=8/5≤2δ22\lvert T\rvert^{2}/5 = 8/5 \le 2\delta^{2} is met by δ=9/10\delta = 9/10.

  3. Adding vertices, higher-order differences, or finite shift-polynomial combinations on the same ray buys nothing, because integrality transports affinely along every ray H↦kHH \mapsto kH: the four-hit diamond Hit(H)∧Hit(pH)∧Hit(qH)∧Hit(pqH)\mathrm{Hit}(H) \wedge \mathrm{Hit}(pH) \wedge \mathrm{Hit}(qH) \wedge \mathrm{Hit}(pqH) is equivalent to Hit(H)\mathrm{Hit}(H) alone, with no primality used ().

Rules out: “find an easier waypoint” as a strategy class. Does not rule out: targets over a with no sample choice, and targets demanding a that irrationality does not supply. These two exemptions are read off the collapse proofs themselves and are exactly what the surviving routes in § exploit. coord:binary-digit scale:cofinal [Lean]

Proposition 17 (B3, no free promotion). Status: observed pattern (an audit, not a theorem). Across the corpus’s proved results, no bounded or partial result has a proof uniform enough to be promoted to cofinal scale by routine strengthening — raising a bound, widening a hypothesis, or reindexing a quantifier. Method: 5656 near-miss rows were catalogued against the four open obligations; 1818 were flagged promotable on a statement-level read; all 1818 proof were then opened. Verdict: 1616 conclusively not promotable with a named blocker each, and 22 promotable with no new mathematics but both pure restatements that widen a target family without supplying arithmetic content. Blocker taxonomy: hypothesis strength ×6\times 6, scale-only ×5\times 5, coordinate-only ×4\times 4, multiple ×3\times 3. Rows with an outright quantifier-order mismatch were judged unpromotable before the body audit and excluded, so the audited 1818 are the subset. coord:audit scale:n/a [Cert]

Observation 18 (The sharpest signal in the audit). Every not-promotable #249-supply row asks for a fact at a specially chosen index: one large aa with a top-edge residue gap, one qq with a terminal-dominance inequality, one exponent past a=6a = 6, one tt past 6464, one sign at one LCM jump, one prime per LCM height, one KK past 240240. Not one such index has ever been located unconditionally beyond the finite census. The single audited row whose missing input is not of that shape is the first-harmonic gap — an over a block. This contrast is what selects the leading survivor in §. It is evidence, not proof.

Proposition 19 (B4, amplitude versus radius: residue engineering is self-defeating). Status: proved (Lean construction plus an unconditional arithmetic margin). A certificate demands that the window residue sit at distance >N+h+L+2> N{+}h{+}L{+}2 from both 00 and 2L2^{L} modulo 2L2^{L}, and the depth floor forces 2L>2(N+h+L+2)2^{L} > 2(N{+}h{+}L{+}2), so the required amplitude is comparable to the modulus. Any producer that that amplitude by prescribing totient values at engineered positions pays for the prescription in position, and position enters the radius. The corpus’s strongest such construction proves the trade is exactly self-cancelling, unconditionally and at every depth: a two-adic pulse block lands the residue at the arc 2K−1mod⁡2K2^{K-1} \operatorname{mod} 2^{K} — the ideal target — and still cannot fire, because its own defining congruence p≡1+2K−1(mod⁡2K)p \equiv 1 + 2^{K-1} \pmod{2^{K}} forces p≥1+2K−1p \ge 1 + 2^{K-1}, so with N=p−KN = p-K, h=Hh = H, L=KL = K the radius p+H+2p+H+2 exceeds 2K−12^{K-1} for every prime pp and every KK. coord:two-adic-pulse scale:cofinal [Lean]

Remark 20 (B4’s own recorded repair, and its scope). Two further Lean facts show that prescribing is exhausted: the full terminal dyadic staircase is unconditionally impossible — its terminal letter would have to be positive, strictly below a wider modulus, and divisible by it, hence 00 (); and the surviving staircase pins its penultimate letter to exactly 2m−12^{m-1} with 2m<2(2H+J+K+2)2^{m} < 2(2H{+}J{+}K{+}2), i.e. no slack at all (puncturedDyadicStaircase_penultimate_eq_half, TotientActualLcmTopEdgeStaircase.lean:1187). The repair the barrier permits is explicit: impose the half-turn on the rather than on one delta, i.e. ask for cofinally many (h,N,L)(h,N,L) with windowDiscrepancy(h,N,L)≡2L−1(mod⁡2L)\mathrm{windowDiscrepancy}(h,N,L) \equiv 2^{L-1} \pmod{2^{L}} and 2L−1>N+h+L+22^{L-1} > N{+}h{+}L{+}2. What is is the failure of the Dirichlet/CRT residue-engineering family by an explicit exponential margin. The broader reading — that only carry accumulation across the weighted word can produce the required amplitude, since one letter obeys |φ(n+h)−φ(n)|<n+h\lvert \varphi(n{+}h) - \varphi(n) \rvert < n{+}h while the weighted word can reach 2L2^{L} — is an inference from the proved instance plus the linear growth bound, not itself a theorem on disk. [Math]

Proposition 21 (B5, bounded state and local signatures). Status: proved (three Lean theorems, all problem-agnostic).

  1. No bounded or autonomous carry state summarising the history before position mm determines the tail after mm: for a balanced-pulse family whose predecessor state is constant, no decode\mathrm{decode} recovers the radius parameter, and any finite state type needs cardinality ≥⌊m/2⌋+2\ge \lfloor m/2 \rfloor + 2, unbounded in mm ().

  2. Long common suffixes erase predecessor information : two affine binary orbits with different seeds satisfy orbitu(L)−orbitv(L)=2L(u0−v0)\mathrm{orbit}_u(L) - \mathrm{orbit}_v(L) = 2^{L}(u_0 - v_0), so the endpoint residue mod 2L2^{L} is independent of the initial carry ().

  3. Bounded local 22-adic valuation-unit data at fixed precision excludes nothing: for any finite word of odd-unit symbols at fixed precision and any starting carry, a compatible orbit exists with every intermediate state centred inside its symbol’s dyadic radius ().

Rules out: the finite-automaton-computes-the-expansion family outright; any hope of distinguishing two carry histories after a long common suffix; and any contradiction derived from a fixed-precision valuation-unit signature. Growing precision is mandatory, not optional. None of the three mentions φ\varphi, so all three bind #257 identically. coord:carry-orbit scale:uniform [Lean]

UN(i,j)=μ((i+1)/(j+1))U_N(i,j) = \mu((i{+}1)/(j{+}1)) when (j+1)∣(i+1)(j{+}1) \mid (i{+}1) and 00 otherwise is lower triangular with unit diagonal, so det⁡UN=1\det U_N = 1 for every NN and the jet map is injective: no finite incidence-quotient relation exists at any horizon (, mobiusCompanionJetMap_injective at :77).

Additionally, every strict-subrank monomial quotient in the Möbius–Mersenne ladder overshoots its target by more than 1/4801/480, — every rung r≥3r \ge 3 lies in [1429/1512,1)[1429/1512, 1) and every prefix after four atoms is within 1/35841/3584 of its rung, so this is a uniform no-go rather than a census (). Its correct reading is the one the source module gives: any winning finite-linear shortcut must live in a genuinely different coordinate or use a growing-parameter construction. Proposition 23 (B7, the coarse-invariant barrier). Status: proved (Lean, #print axioms clean). This is Proposition  read as an elimination. Rules out: any proof of #249 whose hypothesis set on the coefficient word lies inside {uniform boundedness, c(n)≤nc(n) \le n, agreement with φ\varphi mod 22 at every index, failure of eventual periodicity in any strength up to arbitrarily long, arbitrarily separated blocks}. The witness satisfies every one of those and is rational. Does not rule out: arguments using actual quantitative totient size or residue information. That complement is precisely why the corpus’s standing lesson is that only a quantitative argument in the actual-LCM or fixed-rank style can close #249. Any future sufficient condition stated purely in terms of coefficient-word properties must be checked against this fixture before being trusted, for either problem. coord:coefficient-word scale:uniform [Lean]

The shape

Put together, the barriers say something more specific than “the problem is hard”. The certificate residue is a weighted accumulation over an unboundedly long window at full arithmetic resolution, and : bounding the window (B1), coarsening the values (B7), compressing the state (B5), truncating the rank (B6), or letting the prover pick the sample (B2). B4 closes the remaining escape — buying the amplitude by construction — with an explicit exponential margin, and B3 records that in practice nothing bounded has ever promoted.

There is exactly one known way to hold unbounded range and full resolution at once without a finite bookkeeping device: stop naming an index and assert an average instead. That is what an exponential-sum bound is. It is why the surviving routes of § are, with the honest exceptions noted there, the ones that never name a good index.

What the wall does not block

An elimination is only worth the paper it is written on if it leaves somewhere to stand. This section is that payoff. Five routes survive the classification of §; for each we state the exact statement it needs, which barrier it evades, and the evasion is structural rather than accidental. Two of the five are demoted explicitly, because they evade every barrier while sitting squarely inside the class that the strongest pattern (Observation ) indicts. None of the five is a proof, and none is close to one; what has changed is that the space of things to try is no longer large.

  • B4. The statistic is the first additive character of the weighted word, never an individual letter. Nothing is prescribed at any position, so the self-defeating cost that kills Dirichlet residue engineering does not arise. B4’s own recorded repair (Remark ) is to impose the structure on the word rather than on one delta, which is exactly what a block exponential-sum bound does.

  • B5, B6, B7. No carry state is summarised and no fixed precision is used; the estimate is on the true residue mod 2L2^{L} with L→∞L \to \infty. A cancellation bound is not a rank statement and seeks no finite-dimensional relation. And the estimate uses the actual real residue, not parity, boundedness or aperiodicity, so neither countermodel touches it — both differ from φ\varphi at exactly the large indices where this sum lives.

  • B3. The audit’s own verdict on this row is that the consumer side is and already at the obligation’s exact quantifier shape: XX is free, so applying the bound at X≥N0X \ge N_0 gives ∃N≥N0∃L\exists N \ge N_0 \exists L directly. The constants 9/109/10, π/8\pi/8 and 1616 are absolute and do not degrade with XX, hh or LL; there is no case analysis and no table.

Remark 25 (Does B1 this route? No.). It is tempting to say the finite-inspection theorem points at analysis. It does not. B1 says any proof must use φ\varphi at unbounded indices — a necessary condition satisfied by open route here (the LCM diagonal as t→∞t \to \infty, the actual-LCM supply for a≥8a \ge 8, the Farey growth law as K→∞K \to \infty, the rank bound for all ee). B1 does not discriminate. What selects this route is a sharper pair: (1) B4, proved, kills the only mechanism the corpus ever found for reaching full resolution at unbounded range by values, and its own stated repair is accumulation over the word — which is what an exponential sum measures; and (2) Observation , an observed pattern and not a theorem, shows that every single-index producer has failed to be supplied at even one large index, while this route’s missing input is a block average and therefore never requires naming a good index. B1’s real contribution is narrower but still load-bearing: it proves that the finite deposits can never be extended into a proof, so the gap between the census and the obligation is a gap in kind, not in degree. That is a genuine no-go about method, of the same species as a relativization barrier. It is not a selector.

How to use this document

Evidence bands.

Every claim carries one, and they are never blurred. [Lean] means kernel-checked, with the declaration named and the file:line given. [Cert] means an exact finite computation, valid exactly on the stated range. [Math] means ordinary mathematics, proved here or elsewhere but not formalised — Theorem  is the important instance, and its unformalised composition step is flagged where it occurs. [Cited] means published, with the reference. [Open] means not proved, by anyone, anywhere. A proved no-go and an audit over a corpus are both valuable and are never conflated: B1, B2, B4, B5, B6 and B7 are proved eliminations; B3 is an audit and is labelled as evidence every time it is used.

The scale axis.

This is the load-bearing axis of the whole document. scale:fixed means one instance; scale:bounded means every instance up to an explicit bound; scale:cofinal means infinitely often past every threshold; scale:uniform means for all parameters with no dependence. The single most important structural fact about the corpus is narrower: every direct certificate deposit for Sep\mathrm{Sep} is fixed or bounded, although the corpus also contains uniform and cofinal structural theorems. Those stronger-scale results do not produce Sep\mathrm{Sep}. Theorem  says that no accumulation of bounded verification, at any bound, is evidence that the cofinal statement holds. Read every result’s scale tag before reading its content.

Coordinates, and why obstructions are relative to them.

Every obstruction carries a coord tag, because an obstruction is always an obstruction , never a property of the object. The γ\gamma-splice obstructs arguments in the coord:binary-digit coordinate; the rank floor lives in coord:carry-rank; positivity lives in coord:actual-lcm; the Farey exclusion lives in coord:farey. Two consequences follow, and both matter for anyone attacking the problem. First, before reporting a new wall, name the coordinate it was met in and test a re-representation. Second, an obstruction proved in one coordinate is silent about another: Survivor 5 survives precisely because it is coordinate-disjoint from the certificate lane, and Survivor 1 survives because the first-harmonic coordinate is the one in which the corpus’s proved collapse mechanism has no purchase.

Map of what follows.

The premise catalogue records, for each coordinate, the exact statements the corpus holds, with hypotheses, evidence band, scale, and Lean declaration. It is followed by the typed-implication tables (which statement feeds which, and at which quantifier shape), the near-miss index against the open obligations, and the promotion audit whose verdicts are summarised as B3. Nothing after this point restates the barriers; they are all here.

Read this in full before starting.

That instruction is not politeness. The recurring practical failure of this programme has not been a shortage of ideas; it has been rediscovering the same reformulations, because no single document held the whole picture. Every dead route in § was found more than once. If you are about to prescribe totient values at engineered positions, read B4 first. If you are about to define a bounded carry state, read B5. If you are about to look for a weaker sufficient condition, read B2 — there probably isn’t one, and the corpus has already proved as much three times. The purpose of assembling the wall is that the next attempt should start where the last one stopped.

The object, the target, and the exact record

This part fixes the object of Erdős Problem #249, states exactly what is open about it, and records every unconditional numeral, identity and Lean-checked bound the corpus currently holds. Nothing in this part decides irrationality. Every result below is either an identity (no hypothesis, holds unconditionally), a finite computation (holds up to an explicitly stated bound), or is flagged [Cited]/[Open] where that is the honest status.

The object

Definition 31 (The Erdős–249 constant). Let φ\varphi denote Euler’s totient function. Define S:=∑n≥1φ(n)2n=∑n:ℕφ(n)2n,S \;:=\; \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{\varphi(n)}{2^{n}} \;=\; \sum_{n : \mathbb{N}} \frac{\varphi(n)}{2^{n}}, the two forms coinciding because φ(0)=0\varphi(0)=0; the second, ℕ\mathbb{N}-indexed form is the one carried in the Lean source. The series converges absolutely since φ(n)=O(n)\varphi(n) = O(n). Erdős #249 asks whether SS is irrational. This is OPEN. Nothing in this paper decides it; every claim below is either an unconditional identity, a finite computation with an explicitly stated range, or is marked [Cited]/[Open].

Remark 32 (Status). No proof or disproof of Irrational(S)\mathrm{Irrational}(S) exists anywhere in the corpus, formal or informal. What exists is: one large unconditional finite denominator exclusion (§), several exact reformulations of SS that relocate the same open question onto different coordinates without touching its truth value (§–§), and a certificate apparatus whose cofinal supply obligation is the precise open target (recorded in full in Part 1 of this paper; only its finite, checked instances are catalogued here, §).

For every N:ℕN : \mathbb{N}, 2N⋅S=ΦN+RN,2^{N} \cdot S \;=\; \Phi_N + R_N, where ΦN:=∑n≤Nφ(n)⋅2N−n∈ℕ\Phi_N := \sum_{n \le N} \varphi(n) \cdot 2^{N-n} \in \mathbb{N} (the integer prefix) and RN:=∑j≥0φ(N+1+j)/2j+1R_N := \sum_{j \ge 0} \varphi(N+1+j)/2^{j+1} (the fractional tail, totientTail in Lean). coord:binary-digit scale:uniform [Lean]

The unconditional denominator floor

The strongest fact the corpus holds about SS is a lower bound on its denominator should it happen to be rational. It is obtained by a completely elementary Farey/mediant argument, entirely free of any certificate or period apparatus, and is therefore logically independent of the open certificate-supply obligation.

Lemma 34 (Farey gap, fully general). For integers a,b,c,d,r,sa,b,c,d,r,s with b>0b>0, d>0d>0, bc−ad=1bc-ad=1 (i.e. a/ba/b and c/dc/d are unimodular Farey neighbours), and as<rbas < rb, rd<csrd < cs (i.e. r/sr/s lies strictly between them): b+d≤sb+d \le s. coord:farey scale:n/a [Lean]

This lemma is a classical Stern–Brocot fact with zero totient or Mersenne content; it is the generic engine underneath every Farey-gap bound in the corpus, for either open problem.

The same record, transported: the Möbius-square and coprimality-probability forms

The Möbius–Mersenne identity and why bounded coefficients matter

Proposition 44 (Möbius-square reduction). S=∑n≥1φ(n)2n=12+∑d≥1μ(d)(2d−1)2,S \;=\; \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\varphi(n)}{2^n} \;=\; \frac12 \;+\; \sum_{d\ge1}\frac{\mu(d)}{(2^d-1)^2}, where μ\mu is the Möbius function, so μ(d)∈{−1,0,1}\mu(d)\in\{-1,0,1\} for every dd. Consequently Erdős #249 ⇔\iff T:=∑d≥1μ(d)/(2d−1)2∉ℚT:=\sum_{d\ge1}\mu(d)/(2^d-1)^2 \notin \mathbb{Q}, the single reduced target every other result in this subsection and § feeds. coord:mobius-mersenne scale:n/a [Lean]

Remark 45 (Why the bounded coefficients matter — the Erdős-1948 regime). The identity of Proposition  rewrites SS (equivalently TT) as a : the numerator weight μ(d)\mu(d) is bounded, |μ(d)|≤1|\mu(d)|\le1 for every dd, uniformly in dd. This places TT in exactly the coefficient regime of the classical Erdős (1948) near-integer irrationality criterion and of the level-1 sibling identity L(μ):=∑dμ(d)/(2d−1)=12L(\mu):=\sum_d \mu(d)/(2^d-1) = \tfrac12 (rational, trivially) alongside L(1)=∑d1/(2d−1)=EL(1) = \sum_d 1/(2^d-1) = E, the Erdős–Borwein constant, which proved irrational in this same kernel (, [Lean]). This is the opposite regime from Proposition ’s binary-digit coordinate, where the corresponding weight satisfies 0≤φ(n)≤n0\le\varphi(n)\le n and is unbounded. The function φ\varphi has average order 6n/π26n/\pi^2, equivalently ∑k≤xφ(k)∼3x2/π2\sum_{k\le x}\varphi(k)\sim 3x^2/\pi^2, but there is no pointwise estimate φ(n)=Θ(n)\varphi(n)=\Theta(n). A near-integer/Dirichlet-approximation argument of Erdős-1948 shape (formalised generically as and its base-power specialisation , both [Lean], coord:n/a, fully coordinate-free) has a genuine chance of transferring to TT precisely because its weight is bounded, in a way it does not have a chance of transferring directly to the raw φ(n)/2n\varphi(n)/2^n series. No such transfer is proved; § below (cross-referenced here, developed in Part 2 of this paper) records exactly why the transfer has so far failed (the “μ\mu-pollution” obstruction) rather than merely asserting the analogy.

Converters and exact identities

Converters and identities move a statement between coordinates without changing its truth value: definitions, exact algebraic identities, iff-characterisations, and the implication theorems that convert a supply hypothesis in one coordinate into the target conclusion Irrational(S)\mathrm{Irrational}(S). This subsection carries the certificate-kernel core (the Sep(h,N,L) predicate, its completeness iff, and every known reformulation of the open supply obligation) and the Möbius–Mersenne / squared-Lambert identity family, including the Mersenne–Lambert five-row status ladder. Sorted by scale: foundational (n/a) definitions and identities first, then uniform, then cofinal, then bounded, then fixed.

Foundational definitions and identities (scale n/a)

Proposition 151 (The two foundational irrationality engines). Two, and only two, general-purpose irrationality criteria exist in the kernel, and any successful proof of #249 must ultimately instantiate one of them: (i) if u:ℕ→ℚu{:}\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q is eventually never xx and den(uk)⋅|x−uk|→0\mathrm{den}(u_k)\cdot|x-u_k|\to0, then Irrational(x)\mathrm{Irrational}(x); (ii) if ∀q>0,∃m,z:ℤ,0<|mξ−z|<1/q\forall q>0,\ \exists m,z{:}\mathbb Z,\ 0<|m\xi-z|<1/q, then Irrational(ξ)\mathrm{Irrational}(\xi) (with a base-power specialisation bnξb^n\xi matching any digit/carry construction in base bb). Every certificate, cone, or Farey argument in this catalogue exists either to supply one of these two hypotheses or to substitute for them via the 𝚌𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{certifiedKill} route. scale:n/a [Lean] coord:other:dirichlet-approximation

Writing L(f):=∑n≥1f(n)/(2n−1)L(f):=\sum_{n\ge1}f(n)/(2^n-1): L(μ)=1/2L(\mu)=1/2, L(φ)=2L(\varphi)=2 (exactly rational, machine-checked), L(1)=EL(1)=E = the Erdős-Borwein constant, proved irrational in this same kernel; L(A)=SL(A)=S for A=φ*μA=\varphi*\mu is exactly #249 restated in “positive Erdős-Borwein form,” still open; L(Id)=∑σ(m)/2mL(\mathrm{Id})=\sum\sigma(m)/2^m is transcendental by Nesterenko 1996 (cited, not formalised). Any proof of #249 sits on this Dirichlet-convolution ladder next to a proved irrational neighbour (L(1)L(1)) and a proved rational neighbour (L(φ)L(\varphi)); this is the clearest bridge into #257’s native Lambert-series coordinate. scale:n/a [Lean, Cited] coord:mobius-mersenne

Killers and countermodels

Adversarial constructions and no-go results, kept with the mechanism that closes each route so the machinery outlives the framing. Per the corpus’s own doctrine (project memory feedback_invent_dont_audit): obstructions below are coordinate-relative, and each entry names exactly which coordinate or proof-template it excludes, not the underlying object.

Observation 156 (Nonnegative-branch elimination for the true survivor). If the translated actual orbit is integral at the start of Prop. ’s positive corridor, then for every later depth KK with room J+K+(a+6)<2⋅2aJ{+}K{+}(a{+}6)<2\cdot2^a, the negated carry-orbit trajectory −𝚌𝚊𝚛𝚛𝚢𝙾𝚛𝚋𝚒𝚝H(H+J)dK-\mathtt{carryOrbit}\ H\ (H{+}J)\ d\ K is negative and is an 𝚎𝚗𝚍𝚙𝚘𝚒𝚗𝚝𝚂𝚞𝚛𝚟𝚒𝚟𝚘𝚛\mathtt{endpointSurvivor} at every depth in the corridor. This eliminates only the nonnegative branch of the true survivor’s sign — it is emphatically a nonintegrality claim; spurious survivors of either sign may still exist. Any strategy hoping to conclude non-integrality purely from this sign fact fails: Prop.  names exactly what remains. scale:bounded [Lean] coord:mobius-mersenne

Observation 157 (Total dyadic staircase is impossible — route-pruning). For a≥8a\ge8, room bound, and modulus wide enough (2H+J+K+2<2m2H{+}J{+}K{+}2<2^m): 𝙰𝚌𝚝𝚞𝚊𝚕𝙻𝚌𝚖𝚃𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚕𝙳𝚢𝚊𝚍𝚒𝚌𝚂𝚝𝚊𝚒𝚛𝚌𝚊𝚜𝚎aJKm\mathtt{ActualLcmTerminalDyadicStaircase}\ a\ J\ K\ m is false — a terminal window where every one of the last mm letters is divisible by its own growing power of two (2r+1∣letterr2^{r+1}\mid\text{letter}_r) cannot occur. The last letter would have to be positive (Prop. ), strictly below the wide modulus, and divisible by it, forcing it to be exactly 00 — contradicting positivity. Kills outright: any strategy aiming for total dyadic annihilation of the terminal suffix. The generic mechanism (0<e<2m∧2m∣e⟹e=00<e<2^m\wedge2^m\mid e\implies e=0) is reusable wherever a positive quantity is asked to vanish mod a wider-than-itself modulus. The surviving route is the staircase (Prop. ) or the residue-gap producers (Prop. ). scale:bounded [Lean] coord:mobius-mersenne

Observation 158 (The bare 3-rank kernel is exactly tight — a sharpness no-go). 𝚏𝚒𝚡𝚎𝚍𝚁𝚊𝚗𝚔𝚂𝚎𝚌𝚘𝚗𝚍𝙳𝚒𝚏𝚏𝚎𝚛𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎(2n+1⋅2)(2n+1⋅3)=−2n+1\mathtt{fixedRankSecondDifference}(2^{n+1}\cdot2)(2^{n+1}\cdot3) = -2^{n+1} exactly, for all nn (a closed-form computed fixture). The two-adic valuation gained by Prop.  is exactly tight — the normalised 1×11{\times}1 minor is odd at every depth, so the bounded-height primitive kernel alone can never force one additional factor of 22. Kills: any attempt to squeeze more 22-adic information out of the bare 3-rank curvature kernel; further progress needs new arithmetic input, matching the file’s own open target 𝙿𝚘𝚠𝚎𝚛𝚃𝚠𝚘𝙻𝚌𝚖𝙼𝚒𝚍𝚍𝚕𝚎𝚁𝚊𝚗𝚔𝙴𝚡𝚝𝚛𝚎𝚖𝚊𝚕𝚂𝚞𝚙𝚙𝚕𝚢\mathtt{PowerTwoLcmMiddleRankExtremalSupply}. scale:uniform [Cert] coord:other:fixed-rank-curvature

Observation 159 (The parity coboundary countermodel object). 𝚙𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚢𝙲𝚘𝚋𝚘𝚞𝚗𝚍𝚊𝚛𝚢𝚆𝚎𝚒𝚐𝚑𝚝n:=𝚙𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚢𝙱𝚊𝚜𝚎𝚆𝚎𝚒𝚐𝚑𝚝n+2⋅𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎𝙿𝚘𝚠𝚎𝚛𝚃𝚠𝚘𝙱𝚒𝚝n−4⋅𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎𝙿𝚘𝚠𝚎𝚛𝚃𝚠𝚘𝙱𝚒𝚝(n−1)\mathtt{parityCoboundaryWeight}\ n := \mathtt{parityBaseWeight}\ n + 2\cdot\mathtt{largePowerTwoBit}\ n - 4\cdot\mathtt{largePowerTwoBit}(n{-}1), where 𝚙𝚊𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚢𝙱𝚊𝚜𝚎𝚆𝚎𝚒𝚐𝚑𝚝\mathtt{parityBaseWeight} is the eventually-constant word 0,1,1,2,4,4,4,…0,1,1,2,4,4,4,\dots and 𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎𝙿𝚘𝚠𝚎𝚛𝚃𝚠𝚘𝙱𝚒𝚝n=1\mathtt{largePowerTwoBit}\ n=1 iff n=2k+3n=2^{k+3} (lacunary spikes starting at 88). This is a hand-built adversary sequence containing φ\varphi in its definition at all except via its parity. The construction technique — add a zero-valued sparse binary coboundary 2⋅2−m−4⋅2−(m+1)=02\cdot2^{-m}-4\cdot2^{-(m+1)}=0 at lacunary ranks to an eventually-periodic base word, destroying periodicity while preserving the rational sum — is a completely general recipe, directly portable to an analogous #257 adversary matched to 1/(2n−1)1/(2^n-1)-parity patterns. scale:n/a [Lean] coord:other:binary-digit

Observation 160 (What the countermodel refutes — the flagship kill of the batch). There is c:ℕ→ℕc{:}\mathbb N\to\mathbb N with: (a) arbitrarily many, arbitrarily-separated, cofinal explicit “6,06,0” carry pairs (for every N,G,KN,G,K a block of KK such pairs beyond NN, pairwise separated by >G>G); (b) ∀n,c(n)≤6\forall n,\ c(n)\le6; (c) ∀n,c(n)≤n\forall n,\ c(n)\le n; (d) ∀n,c(n)≡φ(n)(mod⁡2)\forall n,\ c(n)\equiv\varphi(n)\pmod2 (exact parity agreement with Euler’s totient); (e) cc is not eventually periodic; yet (f) ∑n′c(n)/2n=3/2\sum_n' c(n)/2^n = 3/2, a number. Kills: any #249 proof strategy whose only inputs are uniform boundedness, the trivial growth bound c(n)≤nc(n)\le n, exact φ\varphi-parity agreement, and failure of eventual periodicity — to cofinal, arbitrarily-separated, arbitrarily-long-block non-periodicity. The obstruction is structural, not a shortage of non-periodicity witnesses: a rational coboundary can carry unlimited aperiodic structure while summing to a fixed rational. Doctrine consequence (matches project memory feedback_erdos_reductions_rejected_bank_real_results): only arguments using actual quantitative totient/Mersenne size or residue information (as in the 𝚃𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝙰𝚌𝚝𝚞𝚊𝚕𝙻𝚌𝚖*\mathtt{TotientActualLcm}\ast/𝚃𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝙵𝚒𝚡𝚎𝚍𝚁𝚊𝚗𝚔*\mathtt{TotientFixedRank}\ast families) can possibly close #249; pure symbolic-word arguments cannot. This countermodel is also the ready-made stress-test fixture for any future sufficient-condition candidate stated purely in coefficient-word terms (boundedness/growth/parity/periodicity), on either #249 or #257. scale:cofinal [Cert] coord:other:binary-digit

Observation 161 (Primitive Mersenne-prime factors alone force nothing). For the completely-multiplicative control c(n)=nc(n)=n (zero totient content: 𝚋𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚛𝚢𝙲𝚘𝚎𝚏𝚏𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕idN=N+2\mathtt{binaryCoeffTail}\ \mathrm{id}\ N = N{+}2): if q>K>0q>K>0 and q∣2K−1q\mid2^K-1 (e.g. qq a primitive prime factor of the homogeneous Mersenne multiplier), the shift is integral at every NN (value exactly KK) but q∤Kq\nmid K. Kills: “a large primitive Mersenne prime factor alone forces a contradiction” as a proof strategy — this is a route-pruning warning applicable to #257, whose denominators 2n−12^n-1 are literally the object q∣2K−1q\mid2^K-1 tested here. Any successful use of such a factor needs genuinely totient-specific residue/size input beyond bare Mersenne primitivity — contrast with the genuinely totient-specific pulse of Prop. . scale:bounded [Lean] coord:mobius-mersenne

Observation 162 (Universal no-go for absolute-adjugate coefficient reconstruction). For any finite rational row w:ι→ℚw{:}\iota\to\mathbb Q, integer targets x:ι→ℕx{:}\iota\to\mathbb N that isolate one totient channel (∑iwiφ(xi)=1\sum_i w_i\varphi(x_i)=1): the crude two-tail cost ∑i|wi|⋅(2(xi+1)+(xi+2))\sum_i|w_i|\cdot(2(x_i{+}1)+(x_i{+}2)) is ≥3\ge3, hence never <1<1. Observation 163 (Rank-2 second-difference certificates: sound but measured not shallower). 𝚌𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝚁𝚊𝚗𝚔𝟸𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕hNL⟹\mathtt{certifiedRank2Kill}\ h\ N\ L \implies the second difference (𝚝𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕(N+2h)−𝚝𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕(N+h))−(𝚝𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕(N+h)−𝚝𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕N)∉range(ℤ→ℝ)(\mathtt{totientTail}(N{+}2h){-}\mathtt{totientTail}(N{+}h)) - (\mathtt{totientTail}(N{+}h){-}\mathtt{totientTail}\,N) \notin\mathrm{range}(\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R), sound at doubled band radius versus rank 1. Observation 164 (Unit-gap strengthening rescues at most one lattice point). 𝚁𝚎𝚍𝚞𝚌𝚎𝚍𝙳𝚎𝚗𝚘𝚖𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚝𝚘𝚛𝚄𝚗𝚒𝚝𝙶𝚊𝚙𝙲𝚎𝚛𝚝uNK:=∀t∈[1,L],¬Coprime(J+t,u)\mathtt{ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert}\ u\ N\ K := \forall t\in[1,L],\ \neg\mathrm{Coprime}(J{+}t,u) (nonunits-only refinement of the Farey-gap consumer). Observation 165 (Synthetic all-horizon countermodel to homogeneous-factor-only proof strategies). There is an explicit nonzero “all-horizon countermodel” sequence built from multiples of φ(𝚙𝚎𝚛𝚒𝚘𝚍𝙻𝚌𝚖t)\varphi(\mathtt{periodLcm}\,t) that (i) agrees with every exact whole-ray anchor 𝚍𝚎𝚕𝚝𝚊𝚃𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝H(qH)=φ(H)\mathtt{deltaTotient}\ H\ (qH)=\varphi(H) for 2≤q<t2\le q<t; (ii) stays inside the natural diagonal bounds; and (iii) survives every finite integer shift polynomial — every commensurate finite-rank LCM cube, via the normal form Pm(EH)⋅∏(EHn−1)P_m(E_H)\cdot\prod(E_H^n-1). This is a representation-level exclusion (a particular factor-ideal projection throws away information that can be adversarially reconstructed), not an exclusion of φ\varphi itself — an actual proof must control the fresh Möbius channel, per 𝚝𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝_𝚎𝚚_𝚜𝚞𝚖_𝚖𝚘𝚋𝚒𝚞𝚜𝚃𝚘𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝙲𝚑𝚊𝚗𝚗𝚎𝚕\mathtt{totient\_eq\_sum\_mobiusTotientChannel} in the same file. scale:n/a [Lean (docstring-sourced)] coord:mobius-mersenne

Observation 166 (Fixed-precision local valuation-unit signatures never obstruct). For any finite word of odd-valuation-unit symbols at fixed local 22-adic precision u>0u>0, and any starting carry state ee, there exists a compatible carry orbit realising that exact word with every intermediate state centred in its dyadic interval (|e′|≤𝚟𝚞𝚁𝚊𝚍𝚒𝚞𝚜uσ|e'|\le\mathtt{vuRadius}\ u\ \sigma). Kills: any proof strategy trying to derive a contradiction purely from “the local valuation-unit signature at fixed precision uu is incompatible with XX” — such signatures are realisable by some carry orbit. Framed against #249 in the docstring, but the theorem itself carries no totient- or Mersenne-specific content: a proof needs growing precision or extra arithmetic coupling, not a fixed-window local signature. scale:n/a [Lean] coord:p-adic

Observation 167 (Square-CRT correction-suppression is independent of nonvanishing). Square-CRT correction suppression (fixing a cofactor mod a prime square to remove a weighted correction term on a finite horizon) is achievable, but suppression alone does not force a nonzero coefficient: the smallest returned countermodel has the whole two-step finite block vanish identically, while a separate clean witness shows it can also be nonzero — “clean” (correction-suppressed) is consistent with vanishing and nonvanishing. Kills: “achieve a clean square-CRT horizon” as a sufficient condition by itself for a nonvanishing correction term; an additional anti-concentration or residue producer is still needed, exactly as the module’s own docstring states. scale:n/a [Lean (docstring-sourced)] coord:other:square-crt-cocycle

Observation 168 (No fixed integer clears every normalised primitive-Euler coordinate). ∀D>0,¬∀n>0,∃z:ℤ,D⋅(A(n)/n)=z\forall D>0,\ \neg\forall n>0,\ \exists z{:}\mathbb Z,\ D\cdot(A(n)/n)=z, where A=φ*μA=\varphi*\mu is the Mersenne-Lambert primitive weight (so S=L(A)S=L(A), Prop. ). Any DD clearing normalised coordinates through horizon NN must be divisible by every odd prime p≤Np\le N, every p2≤Np^2\le N, and by 44 once N≥4N\ge4 — so no fixed DD works for all nn. Kills: any strategy seeking a single fixed integer denominator that simultaneously integralises every primitive-Euler coordinate A(n)/nA(n)/n — a finite no-lift theorem in the integral Euler/Witt-coordinate category (weaker than the general Dieudonné-Dwork theorem, and explicitly itself an irrationality proof). An independent-coordinate no-go, orthogonal to the binary-window (Prop. ) and carry-rank (Prop. ) obstructions — a third distinct coordinate attacking the same open problem. scale:n/a [Lean] coord:mobius-mersenne

Observation 169 (Finite certificates only ever prove exclusion, never membership). Certified-death/kill families (finite decidable checks at a given depth) are explicitly one-sided: a found certificate proves exclusion, but failure to find one, or survival through any finite probed depth, proves about membership or rationality. This is a structural caveat recurring across every certificate family in this catalogue (𝚌𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{certifiedKill}, 𝚍𝚒𝚛𝚎𝚌𝚝𝚎𝚍𝙲𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{directedCertifiedKill}, 𝚜𝚞𝚛𝚟𝚒𝚟𝚘𝚛𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{survivorKill}, 𝙻𝚌𝚖𝙳𝚒𝚊𝚐𝚘𝚗𝚊𝚕𝙰𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚑𝚖𝚎𝚝𝚒𝚌𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{LcmDiagonalArithmeticKill}): none of them can ever certify membership/rationality by finite search, only non-membership/non-integrality. Kills: treating an unsuccessful finite search over any of the certificate families above as evidence toward rationality, or treating a finite prefix of confirmed kills (Prop. , Prop. ) as anything more than a floor to extend. scale:n/a [Lean (structural caveat, cross-problem)] coord:n/a

Recently published declarations

This subsection catalogues material that entered the public record after the rest of this paper was drafted: declarations union-merged into modules that were already public (SignedQMomentObstruction, GenericTailOrbitRigidity, DiagonalFreshLossBridge, SquaredMersenneDiagonalEnclosure, ActualForeignResidueProjection, DyadicPrefixCompression, RepunitMobiusNumerator, GeometricCoprimality, LcmDiagonalReduction, PivotAntiReconstruction, all in Erdos249257/), and the newly published per-problem tree ErdosProblems/Erdos249/. Every declaration below was read directly from source; none is inferred from a name. Several of these files contain long chains of “XSupply →\to irrational” implications whose hypothesis is an unproved cofinal predicate. Per the standing rule of this paper, those chains are named as exactly what they are — reductions, not results — and are not restated as if they narrowed the open problem. The module SquareCRTCube is deliberately excluded: its private additions did not compile even in the private tree and were reverted, so nothing from it beyond the existing public file is cited here.

The Möbius–Mersenne ladder: unconditional log-concavity

SignedQMomentObstruction adds an infinite ladder Θr:=∑n≥0μ(n+1)/(2n+1−1)r\Theta_r := \sum_{n\ge 0} \mu(n+1)/(2^{n+1}-1)^r built from the same Möbius–Mersenne atoms as the rest of the corpus, together with a full unconditional order-two Hankel (log-concavity) theorem for every rung.

Definition 170. Θr:=∑n≥0μ(n+1)/(2n+1−1)r\Theta_r := \sum_{n\ge 0}\mu(n+1)/(2^{n+1}-1)^r, split exactly into the first two atoms TwoAtom(r):=1−3−r\mathrm{TwoAtom}(r) := 1 - 3^{-r} and the tail TailAfterTwo(r):=∑n≥0μ(n+3)/(2n+3−1)r\mathrm{TailAfterTwo}(r) := \sum_{n\ge 0}\mu(n+3)/(2^{n+3}-1)^r. .

Theorem 171 (Two low rungs are exact rationals tied to #249). Θ1=1/2\Theta_1 = 1/2, and Θ2=(∑n≥1φ(n)2−n)−1/2\Theta_2 = \bigl(\sum_{n\ge 1}\varphi(n)2^{-n}\bigr) - 1/2 — the second rung is literally S−1/2S - 1/2. .

Theorem 172 (Two-atom exact Hankel gap). TwoAtom(r+1)2−TwoAtom(r)TwoAtom(r+2)=4/3r+2\mathrm{TwoAtom}(r{+}1)^2 - \mathrm{TwoAtom}(r)\mathrm{TwoAtom}(r{+}2) = 4/3^{r+2}, hence the two-atom truncation alone is strictly log-concave at every rr. .

Theorem 173 (Full ladder: unconditional strict log-concavity, every rung). For every r≥1r\ge 1, ΘrΘr+2<Θr+12\Theta_r\,\Theta_{r+2} < \Theta_{r+1}^2: the shifted 2×22\times 2 Hankel determinant of the whole ladder is negative at every rung, not just asymptotically. The proof propagates the exact two-atom gap above against a geometric tail-error budget that contracts by a factor 1/41/4 per rung against a gap that only contracts by 1/31/3, giving an inductive floor from rung 55 on (kernel-checked base cases below). .

Observation 174. This is a genuine unconditional analytic fact about the ladder, but it is not by itself an irrationality obstruction or a step toward one: negative Hankel determinants say the sequence (Θr)(\Theta_r) is not the moment sequence of a positive measure, which is unrelated to whether any single Θr\Theta_r (in particular Θ2=S−1/2\Theta_2 = S - 1/2) is rational. It is recorded here as exactly what it is — a structural fact about the ladder — and no stronger claim is made.

The file also supplies the underlying algebraic infrastructure: a rectangular Cauchy–Binet expansion derived from the Leibniz formula (, [Lean], scale:uniform, coord:other:hankel-determinant, needed because Mathlib’s pinned determinant API does not expose rectangular Cauchy–Binet directly), and a finite unique-terminal-dyadic-exponent parity lemma showing that clearing a common denominator by its uniquely largest power of two preserves oddness of the numerator (, [Lean], scale:uniform, coord:other:dyadic-parity).

Generic tail-orbit rigidity: a self-labelled non-claim

GenericTailOrbitRigidity is explicit in its own header that it asserts no novelty and no priority, and contains an explicit NON_CLAIM guard against a superseded “positive orbit” route; it is a formal algebra/analysis interface, reproduced here only because it entered the public tree after the earlier parts of this paper were drafted.

Theorem 175 (T7: tempered-orbit equivalence, abstract binary series). For any c:ℕ→ℕc:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N} with c(n)≤nc(n)\le n, writing Xc:=∑n≥1c(n)/2nX_c := \sum_{n\ge 1} c(n)/2^n, XcX_c is rational iff there exist v>0v>0 and an integer sequence uu with u(N+1)=2u(N)−vc(N+1)u(N{+}1) = 2u(N) - v\,c(N{+}1) and u(N)/2N→0u(N)/2^N \to 0; when it exists such an orbit is rigid, u(N)=v⋅Tc(N)u(N) = v\cdot T_c(N) for every NN, where TcT_c is the scaled tail. .

Proposition 176 (Rigidity engine). A real sequence dd with d(N+1)=2d(N)d(N{+}1)=2d(N) and d(N)=o(2N)d(N)=o(2^N) is identically zero. .

Observation 177 (Finite-state no-go for successor decoders). For fixed m≥2m\ge 2, the “balanced-pulse” family cm,rc_{m,r} (mass rr moved from digit mm to digit m+1m{+}1, 0≤r≤⌊(m+1)/2⌋0\le r\le \lfloor(m{+}1)/2\rfloor) has the same value and the same complete pre-mm history for every rr, yet the parameter rr is recovered exactly from the first post-pulse digit. Consequently no state that identifies all members of one such family can be decoded by any autonomous map, and the fan-out of any correct decoder is unbounded in mm. . This is a genuine barrier of the class the brief asks for: it rules out exactly the class of arguments that try to predict/decode the exact tail orbit from a state depending only on the pre-pulse history, because the family exhibited is a literal counterexample generator for any such decoder. It says nothing about the totient-specific series itself.

Two “rational control models” are included as honesty checks, not irrationality statements: the pair-balanced family c(2k)=k−a(k)c(2k){=}k{-}a(k), c(2k+1)=2a(k)c(2k{+}1){=}2a(k) has tempered orbit for every bounded payload aa and a fixed marked value 4/94/9 regardless of aa (, [Lean], scale:uniform, coord:other:tail-orbit-rigidity); and the identity coefficients c(n)=nc(n)=n have the explicit multiplier-one tempered orbit u(N)=N+2u(N)=N+2 (, [Lean], scale:fixed, coord:other:tail-orbit-rigidity).

Squared-Mersenne diagonal enclosure

SquaredMersenneDiagonalEnclosure spends the exactly-summable first-order Lambert term of the actual #249 diagonal exactly, leaving only a squared-Mersenne tail to bound.

Proposition 178 (Exact rational centre, direct). scaleDiagonalTailDifference(H)−lambertProjectedDiagonal(H,D)=CH⋅mobiusSquareTail(D)\mathrm{scaleDiagonalTailDifference}(H) - \mathrm{lambertProjectedDiagonal}(H,D) = C_H \cdot \mathrm{mobiusSquareTail}(D) for every H,DH,D — no residue split and no side condition on DD versus HH. .

Proposition 179 (Sharp geometric tail bound). |mobiusSquareTail(D)|≤4/(3(2D+1−1)2)|\mathrm{mobiusSquareTail}(D)| \le 4/\bigl(3(2^{D+1}-1)^2\bigr). .

Observation 180 (Directed vs. symmetric enclosure). When the first nonzero Möbius channel past DD is known, its sign directs a one-sided interval half the width of the symmetric bound (, [Lean], scale:uniform, coord:other:squared-mersenne-tail), and either enclosure composes with an integer-lattice separation hypothesis into a consumer theorem (). The separation hypothesis itself is exactly the remaining open content; the enclosure is real but does not supply it.

Old/foreign Möbius channel split (DiagonalFreshLossBridge)

The 4243-line addition to DiagonalFreshLossBridge isolates, at the level of individual Möbius-totient channels, which channels are “old” (index divides the LCM height HH) and which are “foreign” (index does not), and proves exact identities for both. Most of the file’s bulk beyond what is recorded here is a long ladder of ...Supply-conditional “⇒\Rightarrow irrational” implications at successively more specialised hypotheses; those are reductions and are not restated as results.

Proposition 181 (Exact old-channel value: a positive gcd word, scaled). For H>0H>0, the sum of totient forward-differences over exactly the divisor channels of HH equals (H/rad(H))⋅gcdWordCoeff(rad(H),s)(H/\mathrm{rad}(H))\cdot\mathrm{gcdWordCoeff}(\mathrm{rad}(H),s), where gcdWordCoeff\mathrm{gcdWordCoeff} is the positive gcd-word coefficient of § below. .

Proposition 182 (Exact old/foreign split of the diagonal height increment). diagonalHeightIncrement(H,s)=oldMobiusIncrement(H,s)+finiteForeignChannelIncrement(H,s)\mathrm{diagonalHeightIncrement}(H,s) = \mathrm{oldMobiusIncrement}(H,s) + \mathrm{finiteForeignChannelIncrement}(H,s), a literal finite-sum identity, not an estimate. .

Theorem 183 (Exact doubling law for the old-channel increment). If HH and rr are both even, diagonalHeightIncrement(2H,2r)=2⋅diagonalHeightIncrement(H,r)\mathrm{diagonalHeightIncrement}(2H,2r) = 2\cdot\mathrm{diagonalHeightIncrement}(H,r); if HH is even and rr odd, the same doubled height increment equals diagonalHeightIncrement(H,r)\mathrm{diagonalHeightIncrement}(H,r) unchanged. .

Observation 184 (Every nonzero foreign phase term is squarefree-supported). A “foreign” channel d∤Hd\nmid H contributes a nonzero phase term to the literal increment only if dd is squarefree and dd divides exactly one of the two window endpoints 2H+s2H{+}s, H+sH{+}s (never both, since d∤Hd\nmid H forces the two endpoints incongruent mod dd). . This is a real structural narrowing — it rules out non-squarefree indices and simultaneous double support as sources of foreign contribution — but it narrows a finite bookkeeping decomposition, not the analytic separation obligation itself.

Proposition 185 (Low/top echo doubling). If a foreign channel dd has a lower-endpoint hit at offset ss, its value there is −μ(d)⋅⌊(H+s)/d⌋-\mu(d)\cdot\lfloor(H{+}s)/d\rfloor, and its top-endpoint value at the doubled offset 2s2s is exactly twice that quantity in absolute value (with sign flipped): foreignChannelPhaseTerm(d,H,2s)=2(μ(d)⌊(H+s)/d⌋)\mathrm{foreignChannelPhaseTerm}(d,H,2s) = 2\bigl(\mu(d)\lfloor(H{+}s)/d\rfloor\bigr). .

Geometric coprimality: a lattice coordinate, and a classical identity beside it

GeometricCoprimality relocates #249 onto the visible-lattice-point mass of coprime pairs. Beside that bridge it formalises the classical gcd-layering identity for the Lambert-weighted coprime sum. That identity is an elementary rational function of its parameter, so it cannot distinguish rational from irrational inputs; and it carries a different summand weight from SS, so it is not a statement about #249.

Theorem 194 (Visible-point count is the totient, uniformly). For every n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}, #{(a,b):a+b=n,0<a,gcd⁡(a,b)=1}=φ(n)\#\{(a,b): a+b=n,\ 0<a,\ \gcd(a,b)=1\} = \varphi(n), with no case split at n=0,1n=0,1. .

Proposition 195 (Coprime-pair lattice mass bridges). For 0≤r<10\le r<1: ∑(a,b)coprime,a≥1ra+b=∑nφ(n)rn\sum_{(a,b)\ \mathrm{coprime},\,a\ge 1} r^{a+b} = \sum_n \varphi(n)r^n; over strictly positive coprime pairs the same sum is ∑nφ(n)rn−r\sum_n\varphi(n)r^n - r; and layering by gcd⁡=g\gcd = g recovers the full positive-quadrant mass ∑g[layer g]=(r/(1−r))2\sum_g[\text{layer }g] = (r/(1-r))^2, which equals 11 exactly at r=1/2r=1/2 (two independent fair-coin waiting times have a finite gcd almost surely). .

Theorem 196 (The classical visible-point Lambert identity). For every 0≤r<10\le r<1, ∑(a,b)coprime,a,b≥1ra+b1−ra+b=(r1−r)2\sum_{(a,b)\ \mathrm{coprime},\, a,b\ge 1} \dfrac{r^{a+b}}{1-r^{a+b}} = \Bigl(\dfrac{r}{1-r}\Bigr)^2, an elementary rational function of rr, hence rational at every rational rr including r=1/2r=1/2. This is the classical visible-point identity, and the Lean declaration is a formalisation of it rather than a new result: writing each pair (A,B)(A,B) of positive integers uniquely as g⋅(a,b)g\cdot(a,b) with gcd⁡(a,b)=1\gcd(a,b)=1 converts the quadrant sum ∑A,B≥1rA+B=(r/(1−r))2\sum_{A,B\ge1}r^{A+B}=(r/(1-r))^2 into the displayed sum over visible points, which is the gcd\gcd-layering already recorded in the bridges above. Its summand weight is the Lambert weight ra+b/(1−ra+b)r^{a+b}/(1-r^{a+b}), not the plain weight ra+br^{a+b} under which the same index set sums to ∑nφ(n)rn\sum_n\varphi(n)r^n; the two sums share an index set and differ in weight, and only the second is SS. .

Observation 197. The consequence to draw is narrow, and it is about the Lambert-weighted sum rather than about SS. Coprime-pair restriction, exact Stern–Brocot-type splitting by gcd\gcd, and geometric cylinder decay of the summand under the map n↦rn/(1−rn)n\mapsto r^n/(1-r^n), used together and evaluated at a rational rr, cannot imply irrationality of the resulting sum, because the identical construction is provably rational at rational rr in [0,1)[0,1) — the mechanism has zero sensitivity to whether rr itself is rational. This closes one route through the coprime-lattice coordinate; it does not close the coordinate, and it is not evidence about the plain-weight sum that actually equals SS. Any future argument built on this specific route must use some further feature of r=1/2r=1/2 beyond coprimality, gcd-layering, and geometric decay.

Cyclotomic anchored kills: unconditional prime support, plus new exclusion certificates

The newly published ErdosProblems/Erdos249/CyclotomicAnchoredKill.lean (3222 lines, namespace ErdosProblems.Erdos249.CyclotomicAnchoredKill) discharges the abstract order-consumer producer of § completely for the concrete polynomial X−2X-2, and separately deposits new kernel-checked denominator exclusions. Theorem 201 (Unconditional unbounded prime support for the Mersenne layer). Every prime divisor pp of 2q−12^q-1, for prime qq, satisfies q∣p−1q\mid p-1 (the order of 22 mod pp is exactly qq, by Fermat/Lagrange in (ℤ/p)×(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times); consequently the prime divisors appearing in the layers {2n−1}\{2^n-1\} are unbounded, unconditionally, with no cyclotomic resultant hypothesis left open. .

These two theorems are genuine unconditional number theory — an exact-order argument and a Dirichlet-plus-cyclotomic-root existence construction — and they close the abstract producer hypotheses of PrimeRayCyclotomicCurvature (§) for the X−2X-2 layer with no residual conditional. Neither result touches the irrationality question itself; they supply arithmetic support for a , still-open cofinal predicate about certified kills at cyclotomic-anchored periods.

Prime-ray cyclotomic curvature: the abstract order-consumer producer

Theorem 205 (Bounded-degree order realisability forces unbounded prime support). If every prime divisor of a layer C(mq)C(mq) has order at most dd in the relevant residue group (BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer), then for every fixed finite set of primes SS, all sufficiently large prime indices qq avoid SS entirely on layer C(mq)C(mq); combined with a nontrivial-layer hypothesis this forces arbitrarily large new prime divisors on cofinally many prime indices. . This is the abstract producer instantiated unconditionally for X−2X-2 in §’s sibling result above; polynomial resultant realisability and Archimedean growth for other layers remain explicit upstream obligations, not proved here.

For every e≥1e\ge 1 and Y≥4Y\ge 4, t(Y,e+2)2/t(Y,2e+2)−Θ2>1/480.t(Y,e{+}2)^2/t(Y,2e{+}2) - \Theta_2 > 1/480. Every rank-one monomial Schur quotient built this way overshoots Θ2=S−1/2\Theta_2 = S-1/2 by a fixed positive margin, uniformly in ee and YY; the bound uses only two interval facts (every rung r≥3r\ge 3 lies in [1429/1512,1)[1429/1512,1), and every length-≥4\ge\!4 prefix is within 1/35841/3584 of its rung). .

For any nonempty finite positively-weighted family of admissible quotients, the weighted average still overshoots Θ2\Theta_2 by more than 1/4801/480; and every primitive integer linear form qΘ2−pq\Theta_2 - p realising such a quotient satisfies |qΘ2−p|>q/480|q\Theta_2 - p| > q/480. .

This is a proved barrier stated at the required precision: the class of argument it rules out is exactly “a primitive rational linear form for Θ2\Theta_2 (equivalently for SS) obtained as a rank-one strict-subrank monomial quotient of finite Möbius–Mersenne prefixes,” and the reason is the explicit uniform lower bound above, not an empirical failure report. It does not touch, and is not claimed to touch, linear forms built by any other mechanism.

The scale ladder

Every statement in the Erdős #249 corpus that this paper draws on is tagged with a : scale:fixed (a finite, explicitly enumerated set of parameter values, typically closed by decide/interval_cases), scale:bounded (holds for all parameter values on one side of a threshold, e.g. ∀a≥8\forall a\ge 8, but the proof or the constants inside it do not survive removing the threshold), scale:uniform (holds unconditionally for every value of every free parameter, with no scale restriction at all), and scale:cofinal (an existential claim of the shape ∀N0∃N≥N0,P(N)\forall N_0\,\exists N\ge N_0,\ P(N) — infinitely often, arbitrarily far out). The source tables underlying this ladder also mark a handful of pure identities and converters n/a when they are not indexed by any problem-scale parameter at all (they are definitions or unconditional equivalences); for ladder purposes these are folded into scale:uniform, since an unconditional statement is, if anything, stronger than a uniform one. This convention is applied uniformly below and is stated here once rather than re-flagged on every row.

#249’s own supply obligation is cofinal. The reduction chain (§, and see ) shows Irrational(∑n≥1φ(n)/2n)⇔∀a0∃a≥a0,𝚊𝚌𝚝𝚞𝚊𝚕𝙻𝚌𝚖𝚃𝚊𝚒𝚕𝙾𝚛𝚋𝚒𝚝a∉range(ℤ→ℝ),\mathrm{Irrational}\Bigl(\sum_{n\ge 1}\varphi(n)/2^n\Bigr) \iff \forall a_0\ \exists a\ge a_0,\ \texttt{actualLcmTailOrbit}\ a \notin \mathrm{range}(\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}), an cofinal statement in the exponent aa that indexes H=periodLcm(2a)H=\mathrm{periodLcm}(2^a). Nothing weaker in scale can close #249; the entire question is whether the corpus’s uniform, bounded, and fixed machinery can be pushed to cofinal. The table below lists every catalogued #249 result, grouped by scale, with a horizontal rule separating everything that is (uniform, bounded, fixed) from the handful of statements that are themselves the or consumers of it (below the rule). Quantifier prefixes are written out explicitly and exactly as recorded against the Lean source; nothing is compressed to “∀…\forall\dots” where the source specifies bounds.

†^\dagger The source normal-form table tags actualLcmTailDiff_shift_pos scale:bounded because the window parameter JJ is finite-range relative to 2⋅2a2\cdot2^a; the exponent aa itself is completely unbounded (∀a≥8\forall a\ge 8), and this row’s constants (44, 88, 3232) do not degrade with aa. It is flagged here, not silently re-tagged, because it is exactly the kind of row an automated promotion sweep must not misclassify — see the audit below.

Checked negative result: no free promotion from bounded to cofinal

A ladder like the one above invites an obvious question: is any scale:bounded result actually uniform in disguise, so that removing its threshold is a routine generalisation rather than new mathematics? This was checked directly rather than assumed. An audit read the Lean proof body behind every bounded-scale result in the #249 corpus — eighteen candidates in total, spanning the near-miss list against the #249-supply obligation catalogued in the interface index (fourteen rows, each independently checked against the exact cofinal target it is closest to) together with the remaining bounded/fixed rows in the certificate, Möbius–Lambert, and actual-orbit banks above — and found no bounded result whose proof is uniform enough in its threshold parameter to promote to cofinal or uniform for free. Every candidate failed for one of three reasons, and the failure mode is worth recording because it is a checked negative result, not an absence of search:

  1. Finite certificate tables. Results such as (28 explicit values of tt through t=64t{=}64, now a strict subset of the aggregate ∀t≤82\forall t\le82 band), (h∈[1,8]h\in[1,8] at fixed depth 16), and (h∈[1,16]h\in[1,16] at exponent 14) are each a finite of independently verified rows, not a single argument instantiated at a free parameter. There is no uniform proof underneath to strip the bound from; each new row is a fresh finite computation.

  2. interval_cases/decide over a bounded range. Results such as (a≥8a{\ge}8) and the entire /top-edge-staircase family (room conditions of the shape J+(a+6)<2⋅2aJ{+}(a{+}6){<}2\cdot2^a) are proved by case-splitting a residue or a divisor structure that is only exhaustively enumerable inside the stated range; the mathematical content genuinely narrows as the range widens, so decide cannot simply be re-run at a larger bound without an exponential blow-up in the search space it certifies.

  3. Constants that degrade with the parameter. The clearest instance is the echo-versus-height wall (prose:echo_versus_height_two_front_wall, §5e–5f of the ambitious-modular-route note): height-optimal ladder families pay quadratic height P(1)∼2K2/2P(1)\sim 2^{K^2/2} matching ’s own growth rate, while height-minimal integer-relation minimizers regrow the echo term ERE_R to match — for every tested family, the two costs cannot both be driven to zero as the scale parameter grows. The interface index records the same phenomenon for HalfRung(J)(J)-shaped truncation rungs: the certificate window B(J)B(J) is driven by LJ=lcm(2,…,J)L_J=\mathrm{lcm}(2,\dots,J), which grows super-exponentially in JJ, so the per-JJ constant degrades with the very parameter the cofinal claim needs to range over — “the hallmark of a proof that does not survive bound removal” (interface index, row d-3a/d-3b).

None of the fourteen near-miss rows against the #249-supply obligation is closed by a scale argument alone either: reading each one’s own recorded exact_mismatch shows the residual gap is a missing (a constant-saving Weyl-sum bound for e1-companion; a one-sided top-edge residue gap for TE-04/TE-05-weakest), never a generalisable proof technique sitting one omega call away from cofinal. The one row where the source tag itself is imprecise — SGN-01, marked scale:bounded even though its underlying exponent aa is unbounded, see †^\dagger above — is precisely the kind of false positive the audit was built to catch, and even there what remains open is the half of the certificate band (the top-edge residue), not a scale defect in SGN-01 itself.

Coordinate atlas and transport maps

#249 is not proved or disproved in a single representation. The corpus expresses S=∑n≥1φ(n)/2nS=\sum_{n\ge1}\varphi(n)/2^n in at least eight distinct coordinates, and the central methodological lesson of the whole programme — flagged repeatedly in the source banks as AP17/AP18, “obstructions are coordinate-relative” — is that a mechanism which kills a proof strategy in one coordinate can be silent, or even actively helpful, in another. This section lists every coordinate used, gives at least one exact transport map out of it into another coordinate with its Lean site, and then makes the coordinate-relativity claim precise for the one pair where it matters most: binary-digit versus Möbius–Mersenne.

Obstructions are coordinate-relative: the binary-digit vs. Möbius–Mersenne case

The clearest instance of coordinate-relative obstruction in the whole #249 corpus is the fate of the classical Erdős (1948) near-integer digit method. That method needs, in essence, a finite automaton: a bounded amount of state carried forward from one digit block to the next, so that the value of a far-away digit block can be recovered from a bounded summary of everything before it. In the binary-digit coordinate this is exactly what fails, and it fails as a proved Lean theorem, not a heuristic remark: shows that for a balanced-pulse family of radius mm, any finite State type collapsing the family to a single autonomous summary must satisfy |State|≥⌊m/2⌋+2|\mathrm{State}|\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor+2 — unbounded in mm — so no finite-state decoder can recover the shift rr from its collapsed state ([Lean], scale:uniform, coordinate binary-digit). This is the formal shadow of the elementary facts that 0≤φ(n)≤n0\le\varphi(n)\le n, that φ\varphi is unbounded, and that φ\varphi has average order 6π2n\tfrac6{\pi^2}n, equivalently ∑k≤xφ(k)∼3π2x2\sum_{k\le x}\varphi(k)\sim\tfrac3{\pi^2}x^2 ([Math]), rather than any false pointwise estimate φ(n)=Θ(n)\varphi(n)=\Theta(n): the digit-window discrepancy windowDiscrepancyhNL\,h\,N\,L genuinely needs Ω(m)\Omega(m) bits of state to track as NN grows, which is exactly why #249’s own binary-digit engine is forced into a () rather than a single finite-state argument: the same shape of no-go recurs at (locked gauge defeats residual-blind rank certificates for the first-harmonic pivot) and at (the dyadic totient-kernel span is genuinely infinite-rank, not compressible to any fixed dimension).

The Möbius–Mersenne coordinate does not carry this obstruction, because it is built on a coefficient sequence, μ(d)∈{−1,0,1}\mu(d)\in\{-1,0,1\}, that is bounded rather than growing with dd. The squared-Lambert transfer engine takes any weight with |w(d)|≤d|w(d)|\le d — μ\mu trivially qualifies with room to spare — and converts it into a divisor-convolution power series for free; no finite-state decoder is ever needed because the relevant recursion (the cyclotomic T1–T6 chain: through ) is a finite, exact polynomial identity at every squarefree radical rr, uniform in rr, with no growth-driven state explosion. This is precisely why the corpus’s strongest denominator result — the exact-value and lower-bound formulas of and — lives entirely in the Möbius–Mersenne coordinate and is scale-uniform, while the sharpest route in the binary-digit coordinate is scale-cofinal and unclosed. The two coordinates are not equivalent representations of the same difficulty: the wall each one hits is a fact about that coordinate’s own state-growth, not about #249 itself, which is exactly the AP17/AP18 discipline this corpus was built to enforce — before reporting an obstruction, name the coordinate it was measured in, and test whether a re-representation removes it.

Interface index: what stands between the corpus and a proof

This section is the join layer of the paper. Parts I–II inventory what the corpus proves; this part inventories, obligation by obligation, exactly what is to turn each proved reduction into a proof of Erdős #249, in a form usable as a premise without opening the Lean tree. Erdős #249 asks whether S=∑n≥0φ(n)/2nS = \sum_{n\ge 0} \varphi(n)/2^n is irrational. It is OPEN. Nothing in this section decides it. Every row below either (a) states a proved theorem exactly, or (b) states an unproved but well-posed proposition (an or ) together with the exact proved consumer that would turn it into irrationality of SS.

Reading this index

Every entry follows the same discipline. Yields: the exact statement proved, with quantifiers in their proved order. Exact mismatch: precisely where the proved statement falls short of the open obligation it is compared against — never “it doesn’t work,” always the named axis of shortfall. What would close it: the exact remaining proposition, stated in full, whose proof (via the cited Lean consumer, already on disk) proves Irrational(S)\mathrm{Irrational}(S).

Each numbered claim carries three tags. scale:fixed means proved at finitely many explicit numerals with no argument in the growing parameter; scale:bounded means proved on a bounded range of a parameter that is itself unbounded elsewhere in the statement; scale:uniform means proved for value of the relevant parameter (the strongest positive tag short of matching the open target); scale:cofinal means the statement itself has the shape ∀a0∃a≥a0\forall a_0\ \exists a\ge a_0, i.e. it is exactly the quantifier shape the open obligation needs; scale:n/a applies to structural non-existence results with no growing parameter. The evidence tags are [Lean], [Cert], [Math], [Cited], [Open], used exactly as defined in Part I.

The canonical open obligation for #249, proved in Part II to be sufficient (), is the 249-supply obligation: ∀h≥1,∀N0,∃N≥N0,∃L,𝚌𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕hNL.\forall h \ge 1,\ \forall N_0,\ \exists N \ge N_0,\ \exists L,\ \mathtt{certifiedKill}\ h\ N\ L . Fourteen near-miss rows are catalogued against it below: one headline row (the sharpest reduction in the corpus, given its own subsection) and thirteen further rows, each attacking the same obligation from a different coordinate.

Remark 219 (Why this is the sharpest reduction, and why it is tractable). This reduction converts the open producer for #249 from certificate-supply language — “exhibit a certified kill (N,L)(N,L)” — into a : exactly the shape of a classical exponential-sum bound in analytic number theory (a Weyl-type estimate for ∑Ne(θN)\sum_N e(\theta_N)). Three features make this genuinely the narrowest gap in the corpus.

First, the saving required is a , not o(X)o(X): 21/2521/25 (complex norm) or 9/109/10 (real part), fixed independent of hh, XX, LL. Any nontrivial cancellation estimate — even one far weaker than square-root cancellation — would suffice; this is not asking for GRH-strength input.

Second, the room condition 16(2X+h+L+2)≤2L16(2X{+}h{+}L{+}2)\le 2^L forces only L≳log⁡2X+5L \gtrsim \log_2 X + 5, which is satisfiable for every XX by simply taking LL large enough (the depth floor grows logarithmically in XX, not polynomially); no scale obstruction of the kind documented elsewhere in this paper (e.g. the 2log⁡2N\sqrt{2\log_2 N} silent-position defect for #257, Part I) stands in the way of the producer’s own room requirement.

Third, the subset form (Theorem ) removes even the requirement that the cancellation happen on the whole dyadic block or a positive-density subset of it: any single explicitly named finite TT with the averaged bound would do. In particular a supplier-fibre or sparse-subsequence argument — e.g. picking NN to be one less than a prime, as the exact pivot algebra in already sets up via pivotArgument, pivotPrime, pivotSupplierBases — is a legitimate route to this obligation and does not need to control the discrepancy on a full interval.

Synthesis: where the frontier actually is

Collecting the fourteen rows, three facts stand out as loci for future effort, stated with the same precision as the rows themselves rather than as summary rhetoric.

First, the single closest approach to 249-supply is the first-harmonic reduction of §: a constant-saving (21/2521/25 or 9/109/10) exponential-sum cancellation estimate, with a satisfiable room condition and, via the subset consumer (Theorem ), no requirement that the saving hold on a full interval or a positive-density subset. This is the only row in the index whose remaining content is recognisably a single classical estimate rather than a compound arithmetic-geometric statement.

Second, the top-edge staircase (TE-04 through TE-05-weakest, coord:actual-lcm-top-edge) is the only row where the corpus has both halved the obligation (one-sided instead of symmetric) and exposed, via the exact identity of Observation , precisely which of two logically symmetric escape branches survives the sign machinery already proved elsewhere in the same file family. That five strictly weaker equivalent or sufficient forms are already proved inter-derivable (Proposition ) means effort here is not fragmented across restatements: proving any one closes the others automatically.

Third, the d4/d5 rank obligation is structurally independent of the residue-coordinate rows above: it is a second, self-contained sufficient condition for #249 (an upper rank bound contradicting the proved 2e−12^e{-}1 lower bound), in a coordinate (carry-kernel rank) where a natural finite-rank strengthening is already proved impossible. A rank upper bound, if found, would not need to route through 𝚌𝚎𝚛𝚝𝚒𝚏𝚒𝚎𝚍𝙺𝚒𝚕𝚕\mathtt{certifiedKill} at all.

No row in this index is a solution, a partial solution in the sense of resolved cases, or evidence that #249 is likely true or false. Every open producer listed is exactly as open as the original Erdős–Borwein question it reduces to; what the index adds is the exact remaining content, verified against the live Lean tree, of each reduction.

Closed routes, with the mechanism that closed them

This section catalogues every no-go, countermodel, obstruction, and refuted proof strategy found in the #249/#257 corpus that bears on Erdős #249 (S:=∑n≥1φ(n)/2nS := \sum_{n\ge1}\varphi(n)/2^n irrational). Erdős #249 is [Open]; nothing in this section decides it. What follows is a machinery inventory: for each dead route, the exact statement that closed it, the exact scope of the closure, and the exact machinery salvaged from the wreckage. The organising warning, stated once here and applicable to every item below: several of these “obstructions” are statements about a of the problem (a proof strategy, a certificate family, a coordinate system) and not about the object SS itself. Confusing the two is the single most common error this catalogue exists to prevent.

Meta-level: finite inspection cannot certify the supply (the γ\gamma-splice remark)

(a) Route as conceived. Every unconditional route to #249 in this corpus bottoms out in a obligation of the shape ∀h≥1∀N0∃N≥N0∃L,Sep(h,N,L)\forall h\ge1\,\forall N_0\,\exists N\ge N_0\,\exists L,\ \mathrm{Sep}(h,N,L) (, the exact open-obligation form quoted throughout the existing manuscript). A natural hope is that verifying Sep\mathrm{Sep} — or its diagonal specialisation — at every scale up to some large, explicit bound BB is evidence that the supply holds, and that pushing BB far enough would eventually amount to a proof.

(b) Exact mechanism that closed it. The manuscript’s own remark ([Math], prose-only, not formalised in Lean: ) gives an explicit splice construction. Take any coefficient stream γ:ℕ→ℕ\gamma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N that agrees with φ\varphi on every index ≤B\le B, and alter γ\gamma at one residue class beyond BB so that the resulting binary series ∑γ(n)/2n\sum\gamma(n)/2^n is forced . Such a γ\gamma exists for every BB (this is the same coboundary-splice technique that produces §’s parityCoboundaryWeight witness, generalised: insert a lacunary zero-valued coboundary edit 2/2m−4/2m+1=02/2^m - 4/2^{m+1} = 0 at some m>Bm>B). Because γ\gamma agrees with φ\varphi on every index ≤B\le B, γ\gamma passes every finite certificate that only inspects indices ≤B\le B — in particular every instance of Sep(h,N,L)\mathrm{Sep}(h,N,L) with N+L≤BN+L\le B that φ\varphi itself passes or fails. Yet ∑γ(n)/2n∈ℚ\sum\gamma(n)/2^n\in\mathbb Q by construction.

(c) Precise scope. This is a statement about , not about φ\varphi: it does not touch SS at all. What it excludes is the inference “Sep\mathrm{Sep} verified up to bound BB, for arbitrarily large BB, therefore Sep\mathrm{Sep} holds cofinally.” The scope is exactly ${\small\textsf{scale:bounded}}$ versus ${\small\textsf{scale:cofinal}}$: any finite-B verification, however large, is compatible with both outcomes, because a rational stream can be built to survive any inspection horizon. It says nothing about whether φ\varphi itself is such a γ\gamma — only that no finite-horizon check can distinguish φ\varphi from a γ\gamma that is.

(d) Salvage. The splice construction is exactly the mechanism underlying §’s Lean-formalised countermodel below, so its is not lost even though this specific remark is unformalised: everywhere a proof strategy in this corpus proposes to certify a supply by exhaustive finite search (the diagonal deposits at t∈{1,…,64}t\in\{1,\dots,64\}, ; the row-200,000 sqrt-escape census on the #257 side), this remark is the standing reason such a search, however large, is evidence and not proof.
